preamble: Method: solve the clues and fit them into the grid wherever they will go, jigsaw-wise.

clue.text: Flier's quarters have effect on us, he repeated

indicators.note: to have an effect on something is to work on it and change it, so these letters get worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps saying that a pilot's lodgings have an effect on the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' throughout this puzzle is a bird; the 'repeated' tells you to write the two-letter pronoun twice before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a bird, and the shed where poultry are kept and roost is their living accommodation.

clue.text: Flier contributing to fax, email etc

indicators.note: something contributing to a whole is only a part of it, so the letters come from inside the following words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second
surface padding, rounding off the list

explanation.surface: A messenger who helps with office communications like faxes and emails.
explanation.walkthrough: The obscure word is fair because it sits in plain view across the two office words; 'etc' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The xema is a genus of gull, Sabine's gull, so it is a seabird and hence a flying creature.

clue.text: Part of Mozambique, a country in Africa

parts.note: five consecutive letters from the middle of the name, stopping short of the Q

explanation.surface: A geography fact: some region of Mozambique is itself an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters do not run on unbroken: the middle of the neighbouring country's name is taken, and then the clue's 'a' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Zambia is a landlocked republic in southern Africa, bordering Mozambique to its southeast.

clue.text: Little boy catches another briefly with caged animals

indicators.note: to catch is to hold, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a short, familiar form of Peter

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: another boy's name, cut to MIC

explanation.surface: A small boy grabs his friend, who is busy with the creatures in the cages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another boy, like the first; the second name loses its last letter before going inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic mice kept by children as pets live in small cages, so they are a kind of caged animal.

clue.text: South American setter, artist without public accessibility

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to himself

explanation.surface: A South American painter who works behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the compiler himself, so ME; RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal Latin phrase: a hearing held privately, in a judge's chambers, with the press and spectators excluded.

clue.text: Flier's mad old spirit to keep up

parts.note: an archaic word meaning insane or furious
old slang for courage, as in 'keep your pecker up'

explanation.surface: A pilot is crazy, an old ghost he must keep in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep your pecker up' is a dated British phrase meaning stay cheerful, where pecker means spirit or courage; 'wood' meaning mad survives only in old texts.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodpecker is a bird that drills tree bark with its beak, so it is a flying creature.

clue.text: Flier — more than one, they say — has power

indicators.note: what people say is spoken and heard, so the spelling follows pronunciation

parts.note: the smallest number more than one
to be able to do something

explanation.surface: A bird, or several of them, is said to have strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, the number plus 'can' gives the bird; this recalls the old Guinness slogan 'Just think what toucan do'.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical American bird with a huge bright beak, so it is a flying creature.

clue.text: Representative of French ambassador

parts.note: a papal envoy or diplomatic emissary

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks for the French envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of French' looks like 'belonging to France' but asks for the French word for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person chosen to act or speak on behalf of a group at a conference is its appointed spokesperson.

clue.text: Joshua's new — dragon's not the same

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to leave something out of the word before it

parts.note: the Komodo dragon, a giant lizard
short for ditto, meaning the same again; removed

explanation.surface: Joshua has something new, and his dragon is not what it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the written shorthand for ditto; taking it off the lizard's name leaves four letters after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua Nkomo was the Zimbabwean nationalist leader, so his surname completes his first name.

clue.text: Flier that's explosive in the sun

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

explanation.surface: A pilot whose plane bursts into flames under the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive; the rhea is flightless, so 'Flier' is a tease here and in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American ratite bird, a cousin of the ostrich, so it is classed among birds.

clue.text: Flier that isn't explosive — always avoid

parts.note: an old or poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: A pilot who's not dangerous: always keep clear of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That isn't explosive' looks like one phrase, but 'that isn't' closes the definition and 'explosive' starts the wordplay; Bombay duck is a fish, not a bird, despite its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name sounds like a waterbird, but it is a small fish from South Asian waters, often dried and eaten.

clue.text: Flier from Mozambique learning to fly

indicators.note: something taken from words comes out of them, here a run of their letters

parts.note: runs across the end of the country and the start of the next word
surface padding, rounding off the picture of a young bird

explanation.surface: A young bird from Mozambique is learning how to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The country looks like part of the definition, telling you where the bird lives, but its last letters start the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: The quelea is a small African weaver bird, notorious in vast flocks that devastate grain crops.

clue.text: Boy holds pole — boy that's got the other — we take boarders

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside

parts.note: a lad who has the other sex's ending, the women's room

explanation.surface: A boy holds a stick while another boy has the rest, and they say they take in lodgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is the opposite sex, so the second boy turns into women. N is the north pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who let rooms to lodgers and provide meals are, by profession, keepers of boarding houses.

clue.text: VP docked without money in Indian capital

indicators.note: 'without' in the old sense means outside, so one piece goes around another
a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Dick Cheney, US Vice President at the time

explanation.surface: A broke vice president finds himself in Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian capital' looks like Delhi, but it means a Native American people whose name is also a US state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheyenne is both a Native American nation of the Plains and the capital city of Wyoming.

clue.text: In Paris you entertain a German — it's full of bloody tubes

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to host them inside your home

explanation.surface: A grumble about a German guest in a Parisian home: it's full of bloody pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' reads like a British swear word about the plumbing, but it literally means carrying blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Veins are the vessels that carry blood, so something with many of them is crowded with blood channels.

clue.text: Annan's dog has sex without restraint

parts.note: Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the United Nations
to bed someone is to have sex with them

explanation.surface: A diplomat's dog mates freely, off the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annan's' stands for the organisation he headed rather than the man himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A curb is a check or limit; when nothing holds something back it is unchecked and free.

clue.text: Flier of flag getting pile back

parts.note: a small flag flown at a ship's bow, as in Union Jack

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, right to left

parts.note: a pile of banknotes or paper

explanation.surface: A pilot in charge of a banner who builds up a heap again.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack is a ship's small national flag, so the Union Jack is Britain's.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small grey-naped crow, a common European bird.

clue.text: Flier's here by chasing a little girl

explanation.surface: The pilot is here, hurrying after a small girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Here alone in the puzzle, 'Flier' means a human pilot, not a bird; 'chasing' puts the following piece after the 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned term for a woman pilot, the feminine form of aviator.

clue.text: Middle Eastern sectary you take to the water in Germany without saying who you are

indicators.note: 'without' in the old sense means outside, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: the German 'See', lake or sea, spelt as it sounds

explanation.surface: A member of an eastern sect takes to a German lake without identifying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside, so the water wraps the identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yezidis are a Kurdish-speaking religious group of northern Iraq; a Yezidee is a member of that sect.

clue.text: Little hair makes stupidity sound half clever

definitions.note: loose: the small sac a hair grows from

indicators.note: a sound is what is heard, so the word is spelt by its pronunciation
half a word keeps just its opening portion

parts.note: the first half of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: Having only a bit of hair makes foolishness seem half smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'seem' or 'healthy', but it signals the spelling-by-ear of the folly word.
explanation.definitionFit: A follicle is a tiny sac in the skin from which a single hair grows; the Latin root means small bag.

clue.text: Fruit not going any distance?

explanation.surface: A puzzle about produce that stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'zero distance', it is nought followed by how far a thing can go.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange is a common round citrus fruit with a tough rind.

clue.text: Flier's a boy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bird of the swallow family
second meaning: a common male first name

explanation.walkthrough: The shortest of clues: the bird name doubles as a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: House martins are small swallow-like birds, and the same word is a familiar boy's given name.

clue.text: Flier on target

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a shot hitting the outermost-but-one ring of a target

explanation.walkthrough: 'On target' looks like an adjective for accurate, but in British rifle shooting it names a particular ring, and the hit scored there.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the pied crow; in target shooting the word names a hit in the ring next to the outermost.

clue.text: Flier using smoother language lacking nothing

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: A pilot whose speech is polished but has nothing to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoother' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun for a tool; O is nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanderling is a small pale wading bird seen running along beaches at the waterline.

clue.text: Flier flown

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bird of prey
second meaning: a toy flown on a string

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flown' must be read as 'a thing that is flown', the toy on a string.
explanation.definitionFit: The red kite is a fork-tailed hawk, and a paper toy on a string is something people send up into the breeze.

clue.text: Flier tied

definitions.meaning: second meaning: something tied in a rope

explanation.walkthrough: Paired with the clue alongside it; 'tied' means a thing that is tied, the loop in a cord.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a stocky sandpiper of shorelines, and a fastening made by looping string is something people tie.

clue.text: Flier turning cold mass to energy

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so it is read right to left

explanation.surface: A physics note: a pilot converting cold matter into energy, like Einstein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass to energy' suggests physics, but 'to' only joins the ice piece to the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving waterbird with lobed toes, found on lakes and ponds.

clue.text: Staccato poem about salt without doubt?

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it
going without something means leaving it out

explanation.surface: A clipped, jerky poem on the subject of salt, written with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: UM is the noise of hesitation. The question mark admits that the definition is a stretch: staccato means broken into separate bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic describes something made of separate, disconnected parts, just as staccato notes are each cut off from the next.
